questions.q: What is the primary function of plant transport systems?
a: To perform rapid locomotion across soil
To move water, mineral ions, and manufactured sugars to all parts of the plant

questions.q: Which tissue in flowering plants transports water and dissolved mineral ions?
Which tissue in flowering plants transports dissolved sugars and amino acids?
In which direction does water and mineral transport mainly occur within xylem vessels?
a: Downward from leaves to roots only
Upward from roots to stems and leaves

questions.q: What substance impregnates the walls of xylem vessels, providing structural strength and waterproofing?
Why are mature xylem vessels hollow and dead cells with no end walls?
a: To store high amounts of active sugar for night growth
To form continuous microscopic pipes that allow water to flow freely with minimal resistance
To trap air bubbles inside roots

questions.q: How are root hair cells specially adapted to maximize the uptake of water and mineral ions?
a: They possess a large surface area provided by their long, hair-like projections
They contain green chloroplasts for light absorption
They are made of solid bone tissue

questions.q: Through which process do water molecules enter root hair cells from the soil?
What drives the transpiration stream, pulling water up from the roots through the stem to the leaves?
a: Active muscle pumping by stem cells
Root pressure and the evaporation of water vapor from leaf stomata

questions.q: What is the continuous flow of water through a plant called?
Which environmental condition increases the rate of transpiration in plants?
a: Warm temperatures, wind, and low humidity

questions.q: What role do stomata play in the transport system of a plant?
a: They pump mineral ions deep into roots
They act as valves controlling water vapor loss and carbon dioxide entry, sustaining the transpiration pull
They seal the plant against all fluid movement

questions.q: How does translocation in phloem differ from water transport in xylem?
a: Translocation moves water downward only using dead cells
Translocation moves sugars in living sieve tubes in both upward and downward directions
Translocation requires no energy from the plant
Translocation occurs exclusively in plant roots

questions.q: What are the specialized living cells that make up phloem tissue called?
a: Sieve tube elements and companion cells

questions.q: Which mineral ion do plants require combined with glucose to manufacture amino acids and proteins?
What is the consequence for a plant if its xylem vessels are completely blocked or severed?
a: The plant grows twice as fast
Leaves wilt rapidly due to a lack of water supply
Phloem transport speeds up to compensate

questions.q: Why do plants transpire, losing large amounts of water vapor?
a: To flood the soil with excess water
It is an accidental side effect of opening stomata for gas exchange, which also cools the plant and pulls minerals
To dissolve insects on the surface

questions.q: How do mineral ions move from the soil into root hair cells when their concentration is higher inside the root than in the soil?
What happens to the rate of transpiration when the humidity of the surrounding air increases?
a: Transpiration rate decreases because the concentration gradient between leaf air spaces and outside air is reduced
Transpiration stops completely for one year

questions.q: Which scientific tool or laboratory apparatus is commonly used to measure the rate of water uptake by a leafy shoot?
What is the primary storage form of manufactured sugars when they reach plant storage organs like roots or tubers?
Where are vascular bundles (containing both xylem and phloem) typically located in a dicotyledonous plant stem?
a: On the outer waxy cuticle surface
Arranged in a ring near the outer edge of the stem

questions.q: Why do plant roots need a constant supply of oxygen from air spaces in the soil?
a: To power active transport of mineral ions into root cells via respiration
To burn xylem vessels into wood

questions.q: What happens to a plant if the soil becomes completely waterlogged and lacks oxygen?
a: The plant absorbs water much faster
Roots cannot respire aerobically, active transport stops, and the plant may die

questions.q: Which factor causes guard cells to change shape and open stomata during daylight hours?
a: Drying out completely until they shrink
Accumulation of water inside guard cells making them turgid

questions.q: What is the structural arrangement of xylem and phloem inside a plant leaf called?
Which direction does sap flow within phloem vessels during the spring when sugars are mobilized from storage roots to growing buds?
a: Upward from roots to growing shoots
It does not move at all

questions.q: What physical property of water molecules allows them to stick together (cohesion), helping pull the water column up xylem tubes?
How does an increase in wind speed affect the transpiration rate of a plant?
a: It decreases transpiration by cooling leaves
It turns water into vapor inside roots
It increases transpiration by blowing away humid air from around stomata, maintaining a steep concentration gradient

questions.q: What is the main function of companion cells associated with phloem sieve tubes?
a: To transport water upward like xylem
To provide metabolic energy and control the loading and unloading of sugars in the phloem

questions.q: Why do plants living in hot desert environments often have reduced, needle-like leaves or spines?
a: To minimize surface area and reduce water loss through transpiration

questions.q: What term describes water loss from a plant that occurs in liquid droplet form at the edges of leaves through special pores (hydathodes)?
Which experiment demonstrates that phloem is the tissue responsible for transporting sugars?
a: Ringing (bark stripping) experiments where sugar accumulates above the cut

questions.q: What happens to the water potential inside a root hair cell when it actively absorbs mineral ions from the soil?
a: Water potential becomes more negative (lower), causing water to flow inward by osmosis
Water potential rises to zero, pushing water out

questions.q: Which feature of xylem vessel walls prevents them from bursting under high root pressure or collapsing under tension?
a: Thick rings or spirals of lignin

questions.q: Why do deciduous trees shed their leaves before winter in cold climates?
a: To make room for new flowers
To prevent freezing water loss when liquid water is unavailable in frozen soil

questions.q: What is the primary source of the water that moves up through the xylem of a tall tree?
a: Rainwater absorbed from the soil by root hair cells
Moisture absorbed directly from air by leaves

questions.q: How does light intensity influence transpiration rate during the day?
a: Higher light intensity closes all stomata instantly
Light has zero effect on water transport
Higher light intensity causes stomata to open for photosynthesis, increasing transpiration
